tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
If we want to find the ratio of two numbers as a percentage, we can use the relationship between multiplication and division.

To demonstrate, let's determine the missing number below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14146952/assets/dfa98ca128e85d05689ed37be0f29dcc2f1f06ae5ee7c930d5ccc76c2564a736.svg)

We can interpret the word "of" as multiplication:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14146952/assets/c5002766655275462fbd346ee2dfba78b1ec4b5e2a603e0e38a2d44f19708cfd.svg)

Now, using the relationship between multiplication and division, we can write our problem as follows:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14146952/assets/72bd81d10d8c50b1ca5d8a9196585d3da7a5d740fd4c75a86e5cd45a87093495.svg)

To write this fraction as a percentage, we write an equivalent fraction with $100$ as the denominator:

$$
\dfrac{7}{10} = \dfrac{7 \times 10}{10 \times 10} = \dfrac{70}{100}
$$

Now we can write this fraction as a percentage:

$$
\dfrac{70}{100} = 70\%
$$

Therefore, 

$$
70 \% \,\,\text{of}\,\, 10 = 7.
$$
